factCheck.applicationToF35B: B-specific visual evidence: the official USMC photograph identifies an F-35B retracting its gear. Its main wheels are visibly forward and above their fully extended positions relative to their strut attachments, supporting forward/upward folding. Direction is a visual interpretation of the photograph; exact trajectory and travel limits are not supplied by its caption.

bRetractionPhotograph.publisher: U.S. Marine Corps / Marine Corps Air Station Yuma / DVIDS
bRetractionPhotograph.title: Simultaneous Launch of Four F-35B Lightning II Aircraft
bRetractionPhotograph.credit: U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. William Waterstreet. DVIDS declares public domain subject to its published restrictions.
bRetractionPhotograph.captionScope: Official caption explicitly identifies an F-35B retracting its landing gear shortly after takeoff.
bRetractionPhotograph.visualObservation: Both main wheels are ahead of their strut attachments in the pictured intermediate pose, with the legs lifting toward their forward bays.
bRetractionPhotograph.inference: The retraction direction is forward and upward. A still image does not qualify exact timing, axes, wheel swivel, or full-cycle motion.

userVideoReference.suppliedObservation: All three landing-gear legs retract forward.
userVideoReference.inspectionScope: Pilot-supplied corroboration; this session could not fetch the YouTube video through its web reader. The independent primary photo and actual-model checks are retained separately.

geometry.frame: Standard glTF: -Z nose, +Y up. Origin below source-FDM assumed longitudinal CG.
geometry.method: Affine transforms of the serialized GLB nodes using the same retained rest-quaternion/local-X binding. Independent retained measurements; production regression test separately evaluates actual Babylon transforms.

actualModelAssertions: Both main-wheel centers move forward and up through four physical positions.
Main-wheel lateral coordinates stay at their authored positions.
Each retained spanwise hinge stays fixed.
Gear returns to its authored extended pose.
A held camera frame does not advance gear motion.
The nose-wheel fully retracted center is forward and above its extended center; its pre-existing forward binding is retained.

limitations: The B-specific primary still confirms an intermediate retraction pose, not a complete gear cycle or exact mechanical trajectory.
The source has no authored gear animation or verified travel limits.
Secondary wheel/strut swivel and exact hydraulic sequencing have not been calibrated.
